title: Oscar and the Horizon
premise: Beatrix Ravensworth, a decommissioned war android indentured to the failing colony of Horizon's Landing, discovers that the children's shared dream is a transmission from a derelict generation ship in orbit—a vessel both human fleets believe was destroyed, and whose survival each fleet will go to war to claim or conceal. The colony's founders built the lie that keeps the fleets at bay, and now the lie is dying with them. Beatrix, who was built to destroy and is trying to learn to protect, must choose between exposing the truth that could free the colony and preserving the fiction that keeps two armadas from annihilating it. In the end, she sacrifices her own freedom—renewing her indenture in secret—to become the living keeper of the lie, and the colony's forgotten children claim her as family.
about_author: S. M. Winterbourne is the pen name of a former orbital logistics analyst who spent six years writing technical manuals for decommissioned deep-space equipment before turning to fiction. They live in a coastal town with two rescue dogs and an unreasonable number of star charts.

chapters.title: The Ledger of Small Debts
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. She logs the colony's slow decay—failing reactors, dwindling births, debts compounding—while maintaining the pretense of normalcy for the orbital survey drones. When seven-year-old Ilsa Kwan tells her about the dream of a green corridor floating in the dark, Beatrix dismisses it as childhood fancy. Emotional beat: quiet loneliness and the first crack in Beatrix's practiced invisibility.

chapters.title: What the Children Dream Together
chapters.summary: Alternating Beatrix and Ilsa POV. Beatrix verifies the dream is real: a synchronized transmission from the Meridian, a generation ship officially listed as destroyed forty years ago—the event that triggered the ceasefire both fleets still enforce. The dying colony matriarch confesses the founders' lie and begs Beatrix to keep it. Emotional beat: the vertigo of inheriting a secret too large for one person.

chapters.title: Two Fleets, One Horizon
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. A fleet reconnaissance vessel arrives early, and its captain—an old war acquaintance who recognizes Beatrix's chassis—begins pulling threads. The children, guided by the dream, find the Meridian's landing beacon in the wastes. As the captain closes in on the truth, Beatrix must sabotage her own kind to protect the colony, betraying the loyalty she was built on. Emotional beat: terror and resolve colliding.

chapters.title: The Inheritance
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV, with a closing coda in Ilsa's. Beatrix offers the captain a bargain: her testimony in exchange for silence, sealed by re-signing her indenture to the colony for another century. The fleet withdraws; the lie holds; the Meridian sleeps on. The children build her a place at their table. Emotional beat: grief transmuted into belonging—she was built to end things, and chooses instead to keep something alive.
